items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: Michael Wolff was not with me then but had been with me for five years.

ctx.x: They got my — and Michael Wolff was not with me then but had been with me for five years. So when Arsenio was out on the road with us it was Michael Wolff, John B. Williams and Roy. So he, Mike was, he always told them, told Michael, that if something happens to me, I’m going to do this and he did and he asked. And I know that the men are real happy about that. And this is one of the most loyal people in the world is Arsenio. So I’m very happy for the guys. John B. is back, Lou Mathews, one of the best keyboard…

felt that he could accompany me as well as Jimmy Jones, you know he loved what Jimmy did for me, that he and he just said I’m not ready. I don’t think I’ll—but he’s been with me now for ten years — so— but that’s the kind of feeling you want from your musicians.

items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you did a 1981 trio album called At My Best with Mike Wolff... Michael was with me five or six years.

ctx.x: Yeah. Because John started laughing and said, “Well I know that’s not going to happen.”

You met him, you married him 30 days later, and you went on to have two daughters, and you kept recording, and you kept touring, and you kept going. Your last two albums for Capitol Records came out in 1980. From then on, the recording pace of the first two decades at least slowed down just a little bit. Between 1981 and 1997 you did a bunch of interesting collaborations and guest spots, which we’ll talk about too. But you also did 10 more albums on your own, six of which I think were produced by Kiyoshi Itoh for…
I’m glad you remember that one. Do you have a copy of it?

items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I did a recording with the boys, the little boy – Michael Wolff’s two little boys... We went in the studio, me and Michael and John B. and Roy.

ctx.x: He stole two of my musicians, yes. I said earlier that John B. Williams had gone to do a t.v. show. That was the television show. It was Arsenio’s show. Arsenio was nice enough to ask me. “I need Michael Wolff and” – so I said, of course.
